title: Are meshy or any other services game ready for 3d models?
author: florodude
selftext: By game ready I mean good enough to use in an indie game with topology in a way that I could animate it and not have it affect performance

comments.author: Practical-List-4733
comments.body: Not even remotely no. You need retopo - usually that comes with retexture and re-UV as well because textures will also look fucked up in some spots or stretch.

replies.author: florodude
replies.body: is it a part of serious workflows at this point?

comments.author: Tyrannicus100BC
comments.body: We’re using Rodin. We rig without retopolgizing. Mesh and textures go right into game (well, sometimes we do minor texture touch up)

replies.author: Practical-List-4733
replies.body: Do you just brute force it with Nanite or what. I cannot imagine that working well.

replies.author: Tyrannicus100BC
replies.body: Works great! Top down 3rd person. Have you tried Rodin? The topologies are super clean. Mixamo usually gets it 90% there, then our artists just fine tune from there.

replies.author: Practical-List-4733
replies.body:
I tried it. The only time it ever looks OK is when you go for ridiculous triangle counts like 500k or something. Like this little Cottage here: 

https://preview.redd.it/ks857a5y2w3g1.png?width=1858&format=png&auto=webp&s=01db4173dbf48047018a4402e0e80c990600882a

It lookd OK when it was ludicrous 650K polys. When I asked it to make it a more reasonable number, it just looks like mush.

Which, btw, 36k tris is still INSANE for this kind of stylized asset, it should be 5-7k MAX, anything above that is just wasting the costumer's processing power.

replies.author: Comfortable_Lunch854
replies.body: That's my experience of Meshy, Tripo and Rodin and can't seems to solve it. Post work in Blender will do nothing or fry the model. AI seems to add thousands or tens of thousands of unnecessary polygons, that can't be simple reduced without it looking like clay. Is there a solution?

replies.author: pierukainen
replies.body: I guess you have a plan with 4k textures? Or the way you use the meshes, they are pretty small on the screen?

replies.author: Tyrannicus100BC
replies.body: No, just using 2k textures. Model resolution is fine. We’re not pushing for ultra fidelity. Aesthetics over graphics. This is the way.

replies.author: florodude
replies.body: what games are you? anything released? and where do you use rodin

replies.author: justifun
replies.body: Hunyuan just released an update to their topology algorithm that's much better now.

replies.author: Still_Ad9431
replies.body: wake me up when there is text to retopo AI and text to uv wrapping... if those AI can't do that, there's no reason to pay 3D AI yet

replies.author: florodude
replies.body: What website is best for this

comments.author: justifun
comments.body: Huynyan 3d just released a new version of their topology algorithm so now you can generate a model.  Segment it into parts of you want.  Texture it and generate quad topology that's pretty decent now.  And you get 30 free credits a day.

comments.author: Financial-Client6167
comments.body: I’ve been using Hitem3D and the performance is decent so far. The topology still needs a bit of time to fix up before actual use, but it meets the standards you're asking about.
